f068.claim: Sangster International Airport serves Montego Bay and handles over 70 per cent of the island's tourist arrivals.

f069.claim: Ian Fleming International Airport serves the north coast including Ocho Rios and caters to private jets, charters and select international flights.

f1014.claim: Canada's advisory states that traffic drives on the left.

f1024.claim: In November 2025 the health ministry advised safe water practices because Hurricane Melissa damaged potable water systems, especially in the west and south.

f1025.claim: The health ministry urged citizens to treat water before drinking it and to follow its advisories.

f1056.claim: The tourist board gives an annual average temperature of 27 degrees Celsius, with the summer hottest and December to March appreciably cooler.

f2001.claim: As of November 2026 the Airports Authority of Jamaica lists three international airports with their codes: Sangster International at Montego Bay (MBJ), Norman Manley International at Kingston (KIN) and Ian Fleming International, listed under Ocho Rios (OCJ).

f2010.claim: Two taxi companies, JUTA and JCAL, operate at Sangster and share an Authorised Airport Taxi desk just outside the Customs exit.

f2011.claim: Sangster's operator says passengers must complete the immigration and customs form before arrival and present valid travel documents, including a passport and, for non-residents, a return ticket.

f2013.claim: At Sangster car hire, hotel shuttles, taxis and the intra-island airlines are in the Ground Transportation Arrivals Hall outside the customs area.

f2063.claim: Canada advises against unmarked taxis because of the risk of robbery and sexual assault.

f2073.claim: The UK advises using tourist-board-approved taxis and minibuses for excursions, airport transfers and sightseeing.

f2084.claim: Knutsford Express runs scheduled air-conditioned coaches between major towns including Kingston, Spanish Town, Ocho Rios, Port Antonio, Montego Bay, Mandeville and Negril, from over 20 locations including international airports.

f230.claim: The official hurricane season runs from 1 June to 30 November, and that period is usually a rainy one even if no hurricane develops.

f237.claim: Hurricane Melissa made landfall as a major hurricane in October 2025, all western parishes suffered significant damage, and some communities remained without electricity and piped water.

f243.claim: Negril is the island's westernmost town, with a seven-mile stretch of beach and cliffs overlooking the sea.

f259.claim: The same strip is also named on that page as Gloucester Avenue, with the coast lying immediately behind the businesses that line it, so a visitor may meet either name.

f262.claim: The tourist board sets out the island's seasons plainly: a tropical wet-and-dry climate, with the wet season running from May to November and overlapping the hurricane season, and the dry season from December to April.

f263.claim: Doctor's Cave Beach is open to the general public as well as to members of the Doctor's Cave Bathing Club.

f267.claim: Montego Bay sits between Ocho Rios, Negril and Saint Elizabeth, which is what makes it a practical base for day trips in more than one direction.

f3014.claim: Canada records the Jamaican dollar as the currency, card acceptance at hotels and tourist businesses, limited cash machines outside Kingston and Montego Bay, and advises carrying enough cash outside those areas.

f580.claim: The foreign ministry's rule on passport validity is that entry is allowed so long as the passport stays valid for the whole of the stay, arrival and departure both falling before it expires.

f584.claim: British citizens need no visa to visit Jamaica and are usually granted entry for up to ninety days.

f589.claim: A customs declaration must be made before entering Jamaica, and the immigration and customs C5 form should be completed online where possible before arrival.

f590.claim: Anything prohibited, or subject to tax or duty, must be declared.

f591.claim: Bringing meat and dairy products into Jamaica is illegal, and customs officers may search baggage and will destroy banned foodstuffs.

f6001.claim: The UK FCDO lists the emergency numbers in Jamaica as ambulance 110, fire 110 and police 119.

f601.claim: As of November 2026 the British foreign office records that access to healthcare in the areas worst affected by Hurricane Melissa is limited, with some areas still working out of field hospitals.

f6047.claim: The JCF gives 119 for police emergencies, free from any phone, and Crime Stop 311 for anonymous information.

f610.claim: Gang violence and shootings occur mostly in inner city areas, and tourist areas are not usually affected by gang-related crime.

f615.claim: The British foreign office advises against using buses at night, and against displaying valuables or leaving them in a car.

f621.claim: A solo traveller is advised to tell someone they trust, at home or at the hotel, where they will be, and to have transport arranged to get back independently.

f626.claim: The advice is to pack your own luggage and carry nothing through customs for anyone else.

f631.claim: A British driving licence can be used in Jamaica for up to six months, and it must be the photocard rather than the old paper kind.

f641.claim: The Canadian government's advisory for Jamaica is to exercise a high degree of caution, because of the level of violent crime, particularly outside tourist areas.

f665.claim: Canada rates the coastal roads as fair but calls driving inland dangerous, listing narrow winding roads, poor maintenance, insufficient lighting, inadequate signage, poor lane markings and hurricane damage.

f669.claim: Canada advises using only taxis ordered from hotels and authorised by the Jamaica Union of Travellers Association, identified by red and white registration plates lettered PP and a lime-green sticker on the window.

f672.claim: Canada advises staying on main roads where possible, driving defensively, keeping doors and windows closed and locked, and leaving nothing valuable within reach or in sight.

f679.claim: An airline's own rules on passport validity may be stricter than the country's entry rules, so the carrier is worth asking as well as the government.

f7012.claim: Melissa made landfall near New Hope in Westmoreland as a Category 5 hurricane.

f872.claim: As of November 2026 the tourist board records that, after Hurricane Melissa, all international and domestic airports are operational and open for commercial flights, and advises visitors to check with their airline for updates.

f873.claim: Sangster is the most convenient point of entry for anyone heading to Montego Bay, Ocho Rios or Negril.

f897.claim: The Blue Lagoon is the island's largest spring-fed lagoon, where cold fresh water rising from below meets the warm sea.

f9000.claim: Doctor's Cave Beach, on the Hip Strip, is a gentle, shallow, fine-sand beach suited to families.

f9004.claim: Doctor's Cave Reef and Secrets Reef are among the best snorkelling spots in Montego Bay.

f902.claim: Dunn's River is one of the few waterfalls in the world that empties directly into the sea.

f904.claim: Water shoes make the climb at Dunn's River safer, and are sold at the entrance for anyone who has not brought a pair.

f9140.claim: The Hip Strip is a full mile of restaurants, entertainment and shopping.

k001.claim: Norman Manley International Airport (NMIA), IATA KIN, is about 19 km from downtown Kingston.
k001.source: primary web page (operator / airport authority / tourist board / GOV.UK), read 2026-11-10

k002.claim: NMIA sits on a peninsula about twenty minutes from Kingston's business centre, bordered by the seventh-largest natural harbour in the world.
k002.source: primary web page (operator / airport authority / tourist board / GOV.UK), read 2026-11-10

k003.claim: NMIA handles over 2 million passengers a year and over 80 percent of the island's airfreight.
k003.source: primary web page (operator / airport authority / tourist board / GOV.UK), read 2026-11-10

k004.claim: NMIA is operated by PAC Kingston Airport Limited, a subsidiary of Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico (GAP).
k004.source: primary web page (operator / airport authority / tourist board / GOV.UK), read 2026-11-10

k005.claim: NMIA has a single runway, 12/30, 2,716 m long.
k005.source: primary web page (operator / airport authority / tourist board / GOV.UK), read 2026-11-10

k006.claim: Car rentals, currency exchange, taxi services and tour operators are in the NMIA Arrivals Ground Transportation Hall; luggage trolleys are free and porters ('Red-Caps') are available.
k006.source: primary web page (operator / airport authority / tourist board / GOV.UK), read 2026-11-10

k007.claim: The drive from NMIA runs along the Palisadoes road with Kingston Harbour on one side and the Caribbean Sea on the other; Ocho Rios is about 90 minutes away.
k007.source: primary web page (operator / airport authority / tourist board / GOV.UK), read 2026-11-10

k008.claim: UK advice: of the two routes between Kingston and NMIA, most people take the Humming Bird route via South Camp Road; there has been sporadic violence in the Mountain View area.
k008.source: primary web page (operator / airport authority / tourist board / GOV.UK), read 2026-11-10

k009.claim: UK advice: British nationals have been tracked and robbed travelling from the airport to private accommodation; be cautious when driving and getting out of the car.
k009.source: primary web page (operator / airport authority / tourist board / GOV.UK), read 2026-11-10

k010.claim: UK advice: if you are unfamiliar with Kingston, do not drive in the city.
k010.source: primary web page (operator / airport authority / tourist board / GOV.UK), read 2026-11-10

k011.claim: UK advice: use Jamaican Tourist Board approved taxis, which display a blue JTB sticker; taxi-hailing apps such as Uber are available in some areas including Kingston.
k011.source: primary web page (operator / airport authority / tourist board / GOV.UK), read 2026-11-10

k012.claim: Kingston was founded in 1692 for survivors of the earthquake that destroyed Port Royal; it is the capital and largest city of Jamaica.
k012.source: primary web page (Jamaica Tourist Board), read 2026-11-10

k013.claim: New Kingston, the business hub, is home to several of the city's hotels.
k013.source: primary web page (Jamaica Tourist Board), read 2026-11-10

k014.claim: Kingston is the birthplace of reggae, and the Bob Marley Museum is where he lived and recorded many of his famous songs.
k014.source: primary web page (Jamaica Tourist Board), read 2026-11-10

k015.claim: Port Royal, a quick ride from Kingston, was once called 'the richest and wickedest city on earth'; visitors can tour the old fort and reach the beaches at Lime Cay.
k015.source: primary web page (Jamaica Tourist Board), read 2026-11-10

k016.claim: Hope Gardens, at 2,000 acres, is the largest botanical garden in the Caribbean.
k016.source: primary web page (Jamaica Tourist Board), read 2026-11-10

k017.claim: Devon House is one of Kingston's favourite historical mansions, known for ice cream and pastry.
k017.source: primary web page (Jamaica Tourist Board), read 2026-11-10

k018.claim: A scenic drive from Kingston climbs into the Blue Mountains, with coffee plantations, cool climate and hiking trails.
k018.source: primary web page (Jamaica Tourist Board), read 2026-11-10

o001.claim: Ian Fleming International Airport (IFIA), IATA OCJ, is in Boscobel, St Mary, about 15 km from Ocho Rios; the airport's own guide gives 14.5 km (9 miles) east of Ocho Rios.
o001.source: primary web page (Airports Authority of Jamaica / IFIA), read 2026-11-10

o002.claim: IFIA is named after Ian Fleming, creator of James Bond; GoldenEye, his Jamaican home where fourteen Bond novels were written, is about 5 km away in Oracabessa.
o002.source: primary web page (Airports Authority of Jamaica / IFIA), read 2026-11-10

o003.claim: At IFIA, customs and immigration are available daily 07:00-19:00, with prior notice required outside these hours.
o003.source: primary web page (Airports Authority of Jamaica / IFIA), read 2026-11-10

o004.claim: IFIA's normal operating hours are 07:00-19:00 daily.
o004.source: primary web page (Airports Authority of Jamaica / IFIA), read 2026-11-10

o005.claim: IFIA lists taxi or coach services hire for transportation; taxis are available on site when required and attract an additional fee.
o005.source: primary web page (Airports Authority of Jamaica / IFIA), read 2026-11-10

o006.source: primary web page (Airports Authority of Jamaica / IFIA), read 2026-11-10

o007.claim: The Airports Authority of Jamaica calls IFIA Jamaica's newest international port of entry and the primary airport for accessible luxury.
o007.source: primary web page (Airports Authority of Jamaica / IFIA), read 2026-11-10
